source: MAFF / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), Royal Government of Cambodia — ខ្សែសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំស្វាយចន្ទីនៅកម្ពុជា (Cashew Value Chain Study in Cambodia), field survey report (250 household respondents across major cashew-growing provinces), 2017, 57pp
text:
Background on cashew nut markets, drawn from the literature review of a 2017 MAFF-commissioned cashew value chain study.

Cashew is consumed and traded in several forms: the raw nut is processed into roasted/salted kernels for snacking and confectionery, cashew oil is extracted for food and industrial/cosmetic uses, and the cashew 'apple' (the fleshy false fruit) can be eaten fresh or processed, though this is a minor use in Cambodia. Cashew kernels are nutritionally valued for protein and healthy fat content (IFC, 2010).

Globally, major raw cashew producing regions include West Africa (Ivory Coast, Guinea-Bissau, Nigeria, Benin, Ghana, and others), East Africa (Tanzania, Mozambique, Kenya), and South/Southeast Asia (India, Vietnam, Indonesia, Cambodia, Sri Lanka). Major processing and consuming markets historically include India, Vietnam, the USA, and Europe. The report cites Vietnam and India as dominant global cashew-kernel processors, while much of Africa's and Cambodia's production is exported as unprocessed raw nut to be processed elsewhere.

As of the mid-2010s data cited in the report, Cambodia was estimated among the world's top cashew-growing countries by area (around 250,000 ha by 2016), but the report stresses that Cambodia's cashew sector is overwhelmingly a raw-material exporter — the source cites roughly 95% of Cambodia's raw cashew production being exported to Vietnam rather than processed domestically — meaning most of the value-added processing profit is captured outside Cambodia.

Total estimated global cashew trade value was cited at roughly USD 1,200 million per year around the time referenced in the source (Padwe, 2011).
caveat: Some specific figures in this source (percentages, price points, yield ranges) were transcribed from a scanned document at a resolution where certain digits were hard to confirm with full pixel-level certainty. Figures are reported as best-effort readings of the source; anyone using exact numbers for decisions should verify against the original report where possible.
